scenes.heading: AEMaaCS Overview (Part 1 of 2)
scenes.narration: Cloud Manager. AEMaaCS Overview (Part 1 of 2). In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What does AEMaaCS stand for?
scenes.heading: AEM as a Cloud Service — Adobe's fully managed, cloud-native CMS offering
scenes.body: AEMaaCS stands for AEM as a Cloud Service — the latest offering of the Adobe Experience Manager product line. It is a fully managed, cloud-native CMS where Adobe handles all infrastructure, continuous updates, and scaling.

scenes.question: What is the main benefit of AEMaaCS being 'always on the latest version'?
scenes.heading: No manual upgrades — Adobe continuously and automatically deploys updates
scenes.body: Because Adobe manages continuous delivery for AEMaaCS, customers are always on the latest version — eliminating the costly and risky upgrade projects that AEM 6.x on-premise customers face every few years. Teams shift focus from maintenance to building experiences.

scenes.question: What handles global content delivery performance in AEMaaCS?
scenes.heading: A built-in CDN (Content Delivery Network) managed by Adobe handles global content delivery performance
scenes.body: AEMaaCS includes a built-in CDN (Content Delivery Network) managed by Adobe. This CDN serves content from globally distributed edge nodes closest to end users, reducing latency and improving performance without any customer-side infrastructure configuration.

scenes.question: How does AEMaaCS handle fluctuating traffic demands?
scenes.heading: Automatic auto-scaling — AEMaaCS scales resources up or down based on real-time traffic
scenes.body: AEMaaCS auto-scales its compute resources automatically based on real-time traffic demand. This eliminates the need for capacity planning and manual scaling — a major advantage over AEM 6.x on-premise where over-provisioning or under-provisioning was a constant challenge.

scenes.question: What does 'immutable repository' mean in AEMaaCS architecture?
scenes.heading: /apps and /libs are read-only at runtime — changes only come via CI/CD pipeline deployments
scenes.body: In AEMaaCS, the application code layer (/apps, /libs) is immutable — it is built into container images and cannot be modified at runtime. All code changes must go through the Cloud Manager CI/CD pipeline, which produces a new immutable container image and deploys it.

scenes.question: What is the mutable content store in AEMaaCS?
scenes.heading: /content and /conf — the author-created, mutable repository content
scenes.body: In AEMaaCS architecture, /content (pages, assets) and /conf (editable templates, policies, cloud configs) are the mutable content stores. This content survives deployments because it is stored in a persistent Azure Blob Storage / MongoDB-backed repository, separate from the immutable code layer.

scenes.question: What is Asset Microservices in AEMaaCS?
scenes.heading: Scalable cloud services that process uploaded DAM assets, replacing traditional AEM workflow processing
scenes.body: Asset Microservices in AEMaaCS use Adobe I/O Runtime to process uploaded digital assets in a massively scalable, parallel fashion. They replace the traditional AEM workflow-based processing pipeline, generating renditions (thumbnails, crops), extracting metadata, and running smart tagging automatically.
